title: Slopes, derivatives and simple differential equations
summary: A derivative is a slope; a gradient drives diffusion; and two equations, y'' = −c and y'' = y/L², produce every carrier profile in week 3.

diagrams.title: Slope, curvature and the two profile shapes
diagrams.tryThis: Move the point along the exponential and watch the slope shrink with the curve itself; then switch to the parabola and see a constant curvature.

checks.prompt: An electron density falls linearly from $5 \times 10^{16}$ cm⁻³ to $1 \times 10^{16}$ cm⁻³ over 4 µm. What is the size of the gradient |dn/dx| in cm⁻⁴?

errors.feedback: You divided by 4 instead of by 4 µm = 4 × 10⁻⁴ cm. Convert the distance to cm first.

solution: Change in density: $4 \times 10^{16}$ cm⁻³. Distance: $4 \times 10^{-4}$ cm.

errors.feedback: Check the sign: with $y'' = -2$ the curve is a hill (opening downwards), so it lies above zero between the two points.

solution: $y = 2x - x^2$, so $y(1) = 1$. This is the shape of a carrier profile with uniform generation and no recombination (book ex. 7.8).

checks.prompt: Which function satisfies $y'' = y/L^2$ and goes to zero for large x?

options.feedback: Right: differentiating twice gives $(1/L^2)\,A e^{-x/L} = y/L^2$, and it decays. This is the minority-carrier profile with diffusion length L.
It does satisfy the equation, but it grows without limit. Physical profiles in a thick wafer must stay finite.
$\sin'' = -\sin/L^2$: the sign is wrong. Sines solve $y'' = -y/L^2$.
Its second derivative is the constant $-2/L^2$, not proportional to y.

hints: Which ones give back a positive multiple of themselves?
solution: Only $e^{-x/L}$ stays finite for large x, so a semi-infinite profile is $A e^{-x/L}$.
